title: AERO: Adaptive Erase Operation for Improving Lifetime and Performance of Modern NAND Flash-Based SSDs
problem: NAND flash erase operations apply high voltage (>20V) for fixed long durations (>3.5ms), degrading cell endurance and delaying user I/O. Existing techniques use worst-case fixed latency regardless of current cell erase characteristics.
motivation: Improving SSD lifetime and performance through adaptive, condition-aware erase operations instead of worst-case fixed durations.
method: AERO performs an initial short erase attempt (1ms) to measure fail bits, then predicts near-optimal erase latency based on the fail bit count. It safely reduces erase latency by leveraging reliability margins in modern SSDs while accurately tracking cell conditions.
key_novelty: Adaptive erase latency prediction based on fail bit observation eliminates worst-case over-provisioning while maintaining reliability.
contributions: Proposes adaptive erase scheme that predicts near-optimal erase latency from real-time fail bits
Achieves 43% improvement in SSD lifetime without changing NAND flash hardware
Reduces read tail latency by 34% on average compared to state-of-the-art techniques
Validates feasibility on 160 real 3D NAND flash chips across eleven real-world workloads
primary_theme: Adaptive erase latency optimization for NAND flash
